note: Shows blocks with a chart per step: each block adds one note, and its own neck puts exactly the notes named so far in play (enable) and rings the one just added (highlight), ending on a tune that uses only those notes. The neck shows the frets, so the text names notes, not fret numbers.

exercise.title: Do, Mi, Sol on the neck, one note at a time
exercise.focus: C major in open position · Do → Do Mi → Do Mi Sol → a tune
exercise.why: Knowing where Do, Mi and Sol sit around the open chords is the map for playing melodies by ear.

sections.text: Only {{1}} (C) is in play on the neck. Find it on the A string, then on the B string, and hop between the two.
{{3}} (E) joins it, ringed on the neck. From each C, find the nearest {{3}} above it. Play the pair, then play it backwards.
{{5}} (G) joins them: it's the open G string. Play {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} {{3}} {{1}} from the low C, then try it without looking at the neck.
Press Play below to hear a short tune made of only these three notes, and play along in the neck view. When it feels easy, switch the view to tab.
